_provenance.notes: The Arctic fisheries management plan (2009) closed the US Arctic EEZ — the Chukchi Sea and Beaufort Sea north of the Bering Strait — to ALL commercial fishing until sufficient data exists to support sustainable management. This was the first PROACTIVE fishery closure in US history — closing a fishery BEFORE it opened, not after collapse. As sea ice retreats and waters warm, subarctic species (pollock, Pacific cod, Pacific salmon) are moving north into former Arctic waters. This creates both opportunities and ecological risks.

arctic_management_plan.plan_name: Fishery Management Plan for Fish Resources of the Arctic Management Area
arctic_management_plan.significance: FIRST proactive fishery closure in US history — closed before any commercial fishing began
arctic_management_plan.area_covered: Chukchi Sea + Beaufort Sea + US Arctic EEZ north of 68°N
arctic_management_plan.species_covered: All finfish — no directed commercial fishing allowed
arctic_management_plan.exceptions: Subsistence fishing by Alaska Native communities continues; recreational fishing allowed
arctic_management_plan.data_threshold: Commercial fishing can only open when sufficient information exists to support sustainable management — a very high scientific bar deliberately set
arctic_management_plan.reason: Ice-dependent species (Arctic cod Boreogadus saida, Pacific herring now appearing, capelin) form the foundation of the Arctic food web supporting polar bears, walrus, ringed seals, bowhead whales, and Iñupiat subsistence. Commercial fishing before understanding these species would risk cascading ecosystem effects.

species_range_expansion.description: Subarctic fish species documented north of historical range due to warming

annual_distribution_shifts.current_documentation: Now regularly documented in Norton Sound, Kotzebue Sound, and southern Chukchi Sea (to ~66°N)
annual_distribution_shifts.significance: Pollock are efficient visual predators — their arrival in Arctic waters could reduce prey available for ice seals and beluga whales

annual_distribution_shifts.current_documentation: Now documented in southern Chukchi Sea during warm summers
annual_distribution_shifts.significance: Cold pool reduction allows cod to move north — they are major predators of crab, shrimp, and other invertebrates

annual_distribution_shifts.current_documentation: Chum and pink salmon now regularly caught in subsistence nets north of Bering Strait in Nome, Kotzebue, and near Barrow (Utqiagvik)
annual_distribution_shifts.norton_sound_salmon_growth: Salmon runs in Norton Sound have increased significantly since 2000 — likely northward range expansion driven by ocean warming
annual_distribution_shifts.significance: Salmon in Arctic bring nutrients but also outcompete native Arctic fish (Dolly Varden, Arctic grayling) for prey

annual_distribution_shifts.current_documentation: Now documented in Chukchi Sea — a food web restructuring indicator
annual_distribution_shifts.significance: Capelin are critical forage fish for seabirds, marine mammals, and larger fish

norton_sound_fisheries.description: Norton Sound salmon and subsistence — the emerging hub of climate-driven salmon expansion

annual.notes: ADF&G 2024. Norton Sound chum runs now equivalent to small Bristol Bay tributary runs. Source: ADF&G Norton Sound area annual management reports.
